Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself. Think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where each doll opens up to reveal a smaller version of itself until you reach the smallest one. To prevent the function from looping forever, it must include a "base case" that acts as the stopping point. Once the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and passes the final answer back up through all the previous steps.
